title: The ten brightest stars in the night sky
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: These ten stars are the easiest to find on a clear night and anchor the constellations around them. Learn them and the sky becomes a map you can read, season by season.

How to hold it: Order by brightness is the hard part, so chunk: the big three (Sirius, Canopus, Alpha Centauri), then the next four, then the last three. Hang each star on its constellation, and the constellation on a picture: two dogs (Sirius, Procyon), a hunter with a blue foot and a red shoulder (Rigel, Betelgeuse). Then go outside: finding Sirius below Orion's belt once is worth ten flashcards.
